8.text: The name of the reindeer is generally taken from its color or from some

9.text: peculiar feature of its antlers. Examples of such names are The-quite-Black-

10.text: One, One-with-a-Cross-Branch-over-the-Forehead, etc. Some breeders give real

11.text: names to a few reindeer of their herds: e. g., Young-Lamut-Reindeer (Tor-

12.text: waˊwaq), — though this name was given to a Chukchee reindeer partly for

13.text: the purpose of increasing its agility through the force of the word, — Mush-

22.text: The term of a reindeer’s life is from twelve to fifteen years, though some

23.text: animals live considerably longer. According to age, they are classified as

27.text: Pêˊêčvak (both male and female), less than one year old.

28.text: Peˊnvel (male) and vañqaˊs˙-qor (female), from one to two years old.

29.text: Krɪmɪˊntɪ (male) and krɪˊm-qor (female), from two to three years old.

30.text: Taačɪmɪˊntɪ (male) and ñêraˊn-ɪg̣rɪˊm-qor ([literally, “two times krɪˊm-qor”] a female), from three

33.text: from four to five years old.

34.text: Ñĭroqaˊulɪn ([one of the third time”] male) and reˊwkut ([“doe”] female), from five to six

36.text: Ñĭraqaˊulɪn (“one of the fourth time”), male only, from six to seven years old.

37.text: Čŭˊmñɪñ (“buck”), more than seven years old.

39.text: The reindeer begins to shed its hair in the spring, and finishes in the

40.text: middle of summer. Well-fed animals start shedding before lean ones, and

41.text: grown animals before younger ones. A herd in good condition will finish

42.text: two weeks earlier than a lean one. The new hair is short and sleek, but it

43.text: thickens rapidly; and in September the skins of fawns are suitable for making

44.text: winter garments. For this purpose skins of fawns are used almost exclusively.

45.text: The fawns are killed at two set periods in early fall, according to the kind

46.text: of fur desired. The late fall fawn-skins are used only for heavy overcoats;

47.text: and the skins of grown animals, for sleeping-room coverings, bedding, and the

48.text: like. For the Russian trade, spring fawn-skins of smaller size, called by the

49.text: traders “vyporotki” (выпоротки), are required. Of these, the black skins are

50.text: more highly valued, and bring almost three times the price of gray ones.
